subject.title: [Feature]: feat: trigger session-memory hook on /compact command

question: Should bundled session-memory archive on manual or automatic compaction, and should that contract use `session:compact:before`, memoryFlush, or a separate continuity/memory-finalization API?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent choice changes lifecycle semantics and transcript retention policy, and it overlaps with existing memoryFlush and continuity-snapshot work.

options.title: Use compaction lifecycle hooks
options.body: Approve `session:compact:before` as the session-memory archive trigger, with explicit privacy, dedupe, timeout, and docs/test requirements.

options.title: Keep memoryFlush as the compaction path
options.body: Treat agentic memoryFlush as the supported compaction preservation mechanism and narrow or close the session-memory hook request after documenting the distinction.

options.title: Design a broader memory-finalization API
options.body: Defer this issue into a larger lifecycle contract that covers compaction, reset, prune, and continuity snapshots consistently.

recommendation.title: Use compaction lifecycle hooks
recommendation.body: Approve `session:compact:before` as the session-memory archive trigger, with explicit privacy, dedupe, timeout, and docs/test requirements.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is tied to both hooks infrastructure and pre-compaction memoryFlush history, making them the best available owner for the product-boundary choice.
